newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs, Poles warn no 2nd class NATO members.
newsitem.headline: Czechs, Poles warn no 2nd class NATO members.

text.p: The Czech Republic and Poland on Friday said they respected negotiations between the U.S. and Russia on NATO expansion but warned against creating a tier of second class members.

In a joint statement issued following a meeting between their foreign ministers at this town near the Czech-Polish border, the two nations also said the talks must not interfere with the schedule for admission of new members to thealliance.

"We trust that requirements for countries aspiring to alliance membership will result from direct accession negotiations and will not become part of any formal alliance obligations toward third countries, in order to avoid any second class membership," the statement said.
Enlargement of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) was the key topic at Friday's Helsinki summit between Russian President Boris Yeltsin and his U.S. counterpart Bill Clinton.
The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are the leading candidates to be invited to join after an alliance summit in Madrid in July.
Russia bitterly opposes the expansion of the former Soviet Union's old Cold War foe to territory once under the sway of the Moscow-dominated Warsaw Pact.
